name: K & F Electronics
old_description: Since 1972, K & F Electronics has been a staple in the circuit board world. As a family business passed down through three generations, we've kept our focus on providing top-notch services for everything circuit board related, from design and manufacturing to assembly and even reverse engineering.
about:
K & F Electronics was founded in 1972 in Fraser, Michigan, a suburb of Detroit. The company remains a third-generation family-owned business, with the founder's grandchildren now overseeing operations. From a single facility, the firm has grown into a full-service provider of printed circuit board fabrication, assembly, and design.

The company produces single-sided, double-sided, and multilayer rigid boards, as well as flex and rigid-flex circuits with blind and buried vias. Materials include FR-4, Rogers, Taconic, Arlon, Nelco, Teflon, polyimide, and aluminum. Assembly services cover surface-mount, through-hole, and box-build work, supported by automated SMT lines rated at 18,000–30,000 components per hour, selective soldering, and hand soldering for special requirements. In-house engineering handles schematic design, PCB layout, bill-of-materials generation, and reverse engineering of existing boards. Additional services include 3D printing of prototypes, wire stripping, conformal coating (acrylic), flying-probe electrical testing, and PCB drilling and routing. All boards pass through a multi-level inspection process that includes AOI, X-ray, and dimensional checks to IPC Class 3.

K & F Electronics serves customers needing quick-turn prototypes and production quantities, offering expedited lead times from 24 hours to four weeks. The firm can begin assembly the same day the final component arrives. Its client base includes original equipment manufacturers and contract manufacturers across the electronics sector, though specific industry verticals are not publicly listed.

The company emphasizes its integrated design-through-assembly model, a return rate below 1 percent, and a one-year warranty on all PCBs and PCBAs. ITAR registration since 2009 and ISO 9001:2015 certification support work with defense and regulated customers. The family legacy and same-day assembly capability are cited as key differentiators.

name: KOA Speer Electronics Inc
old_description: KOA Speer's family of current sense resistors offer excellent large current detection due to its metal plate technology. Wide range of sizes, power ratings and resistance values are ideal for controlling the current to protect power supply circuits.
about:
KOA Speer Electronics Inc operates from Bradford, Pennsylvania, where it develops and manufactures a range of passive electronic components. The company positions itself as a passive component partner for designers seeking resistors with specialized performance characteristics.

Its product portfolio centers on resistor technologies built for demanding environments. Current sense resistors use a metal plate structure to handle large current detection across multiple sizes, power ratings, and resistance values. The SG73 series of thick film resistors addresses surge and pulse voltage protection, while thin film lines such as RN73R, RN73H, and the wide terminal WN73H deliver high precision for automotive and industrial circuits. Wide terminal chip resistors employ a reverse geometry that improves heat dissipation and enables higher power ratings in the same footprint. Anti-sulfur variants incorporate a sulfuration-proof inner electrode and metal glaze thick film, qualified to AEC-Q200 and ASTM-B809 standards.

The company serves primarily the automotive and industrial electronics sectors, supplying components that meet automotive reliability requirements such as AEC-Q200. Its resistors are designed into power supply protection, circuit control, and high-reliability applications where sulfuration resistance and pulse withstand capability are critical.

KOA Speer differentiates itself through its metal plate current sense technology, wide terminal architecture for thermal performance, and a focus on anti-sulfur solutions that address silver electrode degradation in harsh environments. The firm also emphasizes sample availability for design validation.

name: KW Solar Solutions, Inc
old_description: Since 2004, KW Solar Solutions, Inc has helped hundreds of customers power their homes through solar energy. We offer photovoltaic (PV) energy systems for homes and other residential properties in Maryland & Delaware
about:
KW Solar Solutions, Inc. was founded in 2004 as a family-owned business in Elkton, Maryland. Dale Wolf, the company’s president and CEO, is an original founder and owner-operator who holds NABCEP certification as both a solar installer and electrician. The firm began with a focus on bringing photovoltaic energy systems to residential customers in the Mid-Atlantic region.

The company designs, installs, and maintains solar photovoltaic systems for residential, commercial, and agricultural clients across Maryland, Delaware, and southern Chester County, Pennsylvania. Its in-house team of master electricians handles every step — custom system design, permitting, utility interconnection agreements, grant applications, and physical installation — without subcontracting. Services also include solar panel repair and replacement, system monitoring, battery backup installation, pest guard fitting, and remove-and-reinstall work for roof replacements.

Customers range from homeowners and small businesses to farms, non-profits, and educational institutions. KW Solar Solutions has completed projects in Cecil and Harford counties in Maryland, New Castle and Kent counties in Delaware, and towns such as Oxford, Avondale, and Kennett Square in Pennsylvania. The company also assists clients with obtaining Renewable Energy Generator certification and selling Solar Renewable Energy Credits (SRECs) through SREC Delaware and SREC Trade.

The firm emphasizes its local roots, 20-plus years of experience, and a full-service model that keeps all work under one roof. It uses American-made panels, inverters, and battery systems, and states that every project meets or exceeds state and county code requirements. Wolf’s NABCEP credentials and the company’s handling of all paperwork and incentive applications are presented as key differentiators.

name: Kalas Manufacturing
old_description: Since 1958 Kalas has been devoted to delivering unmatched value to our customers through
about:
Kalas Manufacturing operates from Lancaster, Pennsylvania, where it was founded in 1958 as a small hardware store. The company remains a privately held family business now spanning three generations of the Witwer family, with leadership extending to include all 700 associates who share a collective purpose to improve the lives they touch.

The company manufactures copper wire and cable through a vertically integrated process that begins with copper rod drawn to customer specifications. Its capabilities include product development and engineering with 3D CAD renderings, flexible manufacturing of small variable lots with short lead times, custom packaging and line-sequencing solutions, and a proprietary inventory management system for copper cost control. The Lancaster facility houses state-of-the-art equipment for producing flexible cords (Extra Hard Service, Hard Service, SVT/SVTO) and other wire products built to UL and SAE standards.

Kalas serves automotive (TS 16949 certified), appliance, lighting, and industrial equipment manufacturers, with applications ranging from vacuum cleaners and small appliances to lighting fixtures. Its engineering team works side‑by‑side with customers in the field to develop cost‑effective solutions, and its vertical integration allows tailored offerings for niche markets across a dynamic customer portfolio.

The company differentiates itself through vertical integration that ensures material control and quality at every stage, a family‑owned culture that emphasizes associate wellness and safety (K.A.R.E. program), and environmental stewardship including recycling of all reclaimable materials, VOC‑free inks, and ISO 14001 certification. Copper management programs such as fixed pricing and prior‑period averaging further help customers navigate commodity volatility.
